newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-HINGIS BATTLES THROUGH AT AUSTRALIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS BATTLES THROUGH AT AUSTRALIAN OPEN.

text.p: Martina Hingis, the only leading seed left in the women's singles at the Australian Open, survived a first-set scare on Monday to beat Romania's Ruxandra Dragomir and reach the quarter-finals.
The Swiss 16-year-old, who is hoping to become the youngest grand slam champion in the open era of tennis, beat the 27th-ranked Romanian 7-6 6-1 in 91 minutes.

The women's tournament has been depleted of top names after a weekend of upsets which saw world number one Steffi Graf dumped out. Hingis, the number four seed, is now installed as odds-on favourite to win the event.

But Dragomir, producing confident groundstrokes and sharp volleys, looked capable of another upset in a first set which saw six breaks of serve in the first eight games and ended with a tight 8-6 tie-break.
In the second set, Hingis was back in the driving seat. Her next opponent will be another Romanian, eighth seed Irina Spirlea.
